incident-bot: ALERT — Severity: P1 — third-party cache auth failures increasing (RedisCloud). Automatic paging triggered. https://status.rediscloud.example/INC-4532 :rotating_light:

incident-bot: Symptoms: auth 401/403 on token handshake to managed cache control-plane. Upstream rate-limiting seen; retries backing off. Observed spike at 1845550000, ~30% of cache calls returning 401/403 across eu-west-1.

Samir: Got the pager. I'm on it. First check: are we getting 5xx from our side or 401 from RedisCloud?

Eli: Logs show 401s from rediscloud control plane during auth-init. Sample: `GET https://api.rediscloud.example/... 401 "token_rate_limited"` repeated. Also seeing our rate_limiter fallback kicking in -> downstream 429s to customers.

Priya: Confirmed — spike in Auth errors correlates with spike in our rate limiter metrics. Circuit-breaker paths triggered for token refresh.

Samir: Impact? Which routes/customers?

Nora (CS): Customer-facing: session-store reads for realtime-sessions and rate-limited embedding cache. A few customers reported elevated errors and slow pages for webhooks. I've opened a Zendesk tag and flagged top 5 customers (acct-201, acct-332, acct-987).

Jules: Telemetry: request latency for /v1/generate up ~300ms p50, p95 up 2s in region eu-west-1. Errors: token-refresh 403 -> fallback_kv_cache miss -> backend reauth attempts -> 429s.

Samir: Initial mitigation options: 1) apply temporary token-cache TTL extension (reduce refresh rate), 2) route cache auth to alternative rediscloud region if possible, 3) enable emergency local in-memory token cache for critical routes.

Eli: Quick probe: can we reduce token refresh concurrency? We have a retry storm where multiple workers request token at same time. Suggest singleflight for token refresh and bump token cache TTL to 10m.

Samir: Doing the singleflight change now. Pushing tiny roll to auth-proxy: `git rev-parse --short HEAD` -> `auth-proxy@a3f2b9`. Rolling to eu-west-1 only.

Priya: I'm toggling token cache TTL in runtime config: `runtime.set("cache.token_ttl_override", 600)` — applying to service-auth in eu-west-1.

incident-bot: Deploy started by Samir (auth-proxy@a3f2b9) — 3 pods -> canary -> region eu-west-1.

rediscloud-sys: We see degraded control-plane capacity impacting token endpoints in eu-west-1. Working on capacity increase; mitigation ETA 12-18 minutes.

Eli: After canary, 401 rate dropped from 32% -> 6% in canary traffic. Rolling to remaining pods now.

Samir: Rolling complete at 1845550240. Observed token refresh concurrency reduced and 401s falling. Monitoring for replays.

Nora (CS): Notifying affected customers: short blurb posted to the top 5 tickets: "We've identified transient auth errors to our managed cache provider causing elevated errors. We're applying mitigations; we'll follow up with a timeline."

Priya: Also added temporary rule to increase our internal rate limiter budget for auth calls by 2x for next 30m to avoid our own throttling during recovery: `ratelimit.set("auth_calls", 2.0)`

Jules: Confirming downstream error rate back to baseline ~1845550280. Latency returning to normal by 1845550305. Will keep watch for 1h.

Samir: Next steps: 1) follow-up with RedisCloud support for root cause and SLA impact, 2) schedule postmortem and storage of token refresh traces, 3) remove temporary TTL and ratelimit overrides after stability window.

incident-bot: Handoff: Samir -> Eli for monitoring window (30m). Eli is now on-call for incident follow-up.

Eli: Oncall ack. I'll monitor spikes, keep CS updated. If anything regresses, re-open pager.

Nora (CS): I'll draft customer-facing incident note and schedule a sync with the affected customers for 10:00 UTC.

Jules: Created postmortem skeleton: https://redwood.internal/pm/INC-4532 — assigned to Samir, Eli, RedisCloud-support.

Samir: Thanks team. Leaving notes in the runbook: add caching singleflight earlier, document emergency TTL override, and add a synthetic check for token error ratio.

incident-bot: INCIDENT: mitigated -> status: degraded -> monitoring. Auto-close scheduled in 2h if no regression. :white_check_mark:
